question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: a plain GET of the authorization-server metadata at the issuer the protected-resource document names, with no Authorization header and no cookie

decoded.endpoints: authorization_endpoint https://account.box.com/api/oauth2/authorize, token_endpoint https://api.box.com/oauth2/token, revocation_endpoint https://api.box.com/oauth2/revoke; service_documentation https://developer.box.com/guides/authentication/; op_policy_uri and op_tos_uri both https://www.box.com/legal/termsofservice
decoded.grants-and-methods: response_types_supported [code]; grant_types_supported [authorization_code, refresh_token]; token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported [client_secret_basic, client_secret_post]; code_challenge_methods_supported [S256] and nothing else
decoded.client-identification: NO registration_endpoint and NO client_id_metadata_document_supported, so an agent can neither register itself dynamically nor present a client-ID metadata document. In the taxonomy of this registry's issue #280 (8 issuers advertise a CIMD, 8 only dynamic registration, 3 neither, 1 unreadable, measured 2026-10-16 and re-read 2026-10-20) this issuer is in the 'neither' class
decoded.mirror: account.box.com serves the same document at its own root path, 798 bytes, SHA-256 equal to this one, read in the same minute. Two resource hosts measured earlier in this registry (mcp.atlassian.com, mcp.vercel.com) serve a root document that is NOT their issuer's; this pair is identical, and the equality is recorded because the absence of divergence is also a measurement
decoded.resource-host-copy: mcp.box.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server answers 401 with an empty body rather than a copy, so no comparison is possible there
decoded.documented-flow: the vendor's setup guide has an administrator create Integration Credentials by hand (client id, client secret, redirect URI, scopes), which is what an issuer with neither DCR nor CIMD requires; metadata and documentation agree

finding: Box's authorization server, read keyless on 2026-10-20 at 18:33Z, advertises S256 only, the authorization-code and refresh-token grants, two client-secret authentication methods, and neither dynamic client registration nor client-ID metadata document support. An agent cannot obtain a client identity from this issuer by any machine path: a human administrator must mint one in the Box Admin Console, which is exactly what the vendor's setup guide documents. account.box.com serves the identical document, byte for byte, where two other resource hosts in this registry diverge from their issuers. 798 bytes, 200, no credential sent.
